AES-128-GCM seal, 32 B, rind: 69 ns, 1.00× the fastest; verified: rind's Lean proof, through Aeneas and hand models of the function-pointer dispatch, of the by-8 AES-GCM and PCLMULQDQ GHASH Aeneas cannot translate, and of the SIMD intrinsics as Intel's manual defines them, of its AEAD API's AES-GCM key setup, seal, and open, for every AAD and message length it takes, down to HACL*'s Vale AES-GCM routines and, for seals under 129 bytes and AAD or messages of 2^32 bytes or more, rind's by-8 AES-CTR and PCLMULQDQ GHASH against Vale's gcm_encrypt_LE and gcm_decrypt_LE without their bound of 2^32 bytes, composed with Vale's F* proofs of Gcm_blocks_stdcall, Gcm_blocks_decrypt_stdcall, and Compute_iv_stdcall, of the code Vale prints at HACL* f557259007db, which rind imports, and with rind's HOL Light proofs of its constant-time tag compare
